purpose: Traceable sources used to design real-world-learning-mentor V1. Entries summarize facts in original wording; they are not imported source content.

sources.title: Build skills
sources.license: OpenAI documentation; use as factual reference only
sources.supported_claim: A Skill is a directory with required SKILL.md plus optional scripts, references, assets and agents; Codex uses metadata then loads full instructions progressively.

sources.title: Subagents
sources.license: OpenAI documentation; use as factual reference only
sources.supported_claim: Project-scoped custom agents live under .codex/agents, have narrow instructions, and concurrent thread count can be configured under [agents].

sources.title: Memories
sources.license: OpenAI documentation; use as factual reference only
sources.supported_claim: Local Codex memories are generated asynchronously and may not update after a chat, so they are unsuitable as the sole authoritative learning-state store.

sources.title: STM32F103C8 product page
sources.license: ST website/document terms; factual reference only
sources.supported_claim: Official device family facts include 2.0–3.6 V operation, flash/SRAM variants, SWD/JTAG and listed peripherals; third-party board specifics still require physical confirmation.

sources.title: Organizing Instruction and Study to Improve Student Learning
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Education, What Works Clearinghouse
sources.license: U.S. government publication; factual summary only
sources.supported_claim: The guide recommends spacing, worked examples with problems, connecting graphics/verbal and abstract/concrete representations, quizzing, delayed judgments and deep explanatory questions with stated evidence levels.

sources.title: Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention
sources.supported_claim: In the reported experiments, prior retrieval improved delayed retention relative to repeated study despite confidence favoring restudy.

sources.title: Improving Students’ Learning With Effective Learning Techniques
sources.supported_claim: The review identified practice testing and distributed practice as high-utility techniques across multiple learner/task conditions.

sources.title: How People Learn: Brain, Mind, Experience, and School — Transfer of Learning
sources.supported_claim: Transfer depends on sufficient initial learning, principle extraction, conditions of applicability, varied contexts and active use; assessment and feedback should be part of instruction.

sources.title: The Power of Feedback
sources.supported_claim: Feedback design should be linked to the task/goal, current performance and next actions rather than only delivering a score.

sources.title: Cognitive Architecture and Instructional Design: 20 Years Later
sources.license: Open-access article under publisher terms; cite/summarize only
sources.supported_claim: Worked examples can help novices construct knowledge, while their effectiveness depends on expertise and design constraints such as redundancy and split attention.

sources.title: Worked Examples and Tutored Problem Solving: Redundant or Synergistic Forms of Support?
sources.supported_claim: The reported work supports adaptive fading of worked examples combined with self-explanation prompts as a route from supported practice toward transfer.

sources.title: How Fading Worked Solution Steps Works — A Cognitive Load Perspective
sources.supported_claim: Successively removing worked solution steps can support the transition from example study to problem solving under studied conditions.

sources.title: Self-Explanations: How Students Study and Use Examples in Learning to Solve Problems
sources.supported_claim: Self-explanation is a relevant mechanism when learners study examples and build problem-solving understanding.

sources.title: microsoft/ai-agents-for-beginners
sources.supported_claim: A public multi-lesson course can organize lessons, examples and practice material without becoming an LMS.

sources.title: freeCodeCamp/freeCodeCamp
sources.license: BSD-3-Clause for main repository; verify subproject content separately
sources.supported_claim: A curriculum can represent challenge/certification structure as data and use validation, but that platform scope is intentionally out of V1.

sources.title: exercism/python
sources.supported_claim: A track can separate concepts, exercises, reference solutions and verification artifacts; V1 may borrow separation but not exercises or tests.

sources.title: Aider-AI/aider
sources.supported_claim: Evidence-first, small scoped change and post-change validation form a useful feedback-loop pattern for engineering learning.

sources.title: langchain-ai/langgraph persistence documentation and repository
sources.supported_claim: Separating thread-scoped checkpoints from cross-thread durable data is a useful persistence boundary; V1 implements its own local event ledger instead of adding the framework.

sources.title: openedx/openedx-platform
sources.supported_claim: A full LMS separates authoring and learning-delivery concerns, but its size and license make it a negative scope reference rather than an implementation source.

sources.title: ankitects/anki
sources.supported_claim: Spaced repetition is a distinct product concern; V1 records due review items but does not reuse Anki code, algorithms, content or branding.

sources.title: openai/skills
sources.license: Individual skill license is located inside each skill directory; repository marked deprecated
sources.supported_claim: The repository explains the directory form of agent skills but tells readers to use current plugins guidance for current examples.
